Subject: Redwood model fit evals & benchmark links

Hi Claire / Mike,

Great to meet this morning — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Goal: replace current on-prem two-model stack with a single hosted endpoint for customer-facing summarization and reranking, target 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for short responses (~80 tokens).
- Key constraints: PII redaction pipeline in front of inference, burst TPS up to 120 rps during morning windows, consistent quality (no regressions on top-of-funnel summaries).

Recommended models for initial evaluation (based on your quality/latency targets):
- redwood-13b (float16): best quality baseline; expect ~120 TPS on a 4xA100 Dedicated cluster with 95th pctl latency ~180ms for 80-token workloads.
- redwood-7b-quant (int8/qat): strong latency/cost tradeoff — roughly 220 TPS, 95th pctl ~120-140ms, small quality delta on abstractive summaries (we'll quantify).

I've attached an initial benchmark export (redwood_benchmark_acme_20260605.csv) and a sample prompt set we recommend running (prompt_set_v2.json). Also linking the Redwood-verified performance profile for the two variants: https://app.redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/ACME-2451.

Next steps:
1) If you can share a small sample of representative prompts (50-200), we'll run a focused quality/latency eval this week.
2) We'll run smoke benchmarks against the two model variants and share token-level cost/latency breakdowns and failure modes.
3) If results look good, propose a 2-week pilot on Dedicated capacity to validate burst behavior and KV/prefix caching benefits.

Can you confirm who will own the sample prompt set and whether the PII redaction step will be applied before we ingest samples?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if useful.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--

Thanks Alex — very helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications before we send prompts: 

- On the 95th percentile latency target: our product team requires 95th < 200ms for the primary summary path under steady-state 60 rps, and sustained burst behavior up to 120 rps with graceful degradation. Can you confirm the cluster sizing assumptions that produced the numbers you listed?
- I'm concerned about quality regressions with quantized variants; do you have any evals showing abstractive summary delta (ROUGE/BERTScore) for redwood-7b-quant vs redwood-13b? If not, can you run a small regression check on our sample set?

We'll start preparing a 100-prompt sample (anonymized) — should be ready by Monday. PII redaction will be handled on our side before share.

Appreciate the clear next steps.


Claire

Hi Claire — great, thanks. Quick answers and plan: 

- Cluster assumptions: the redwood-13b numbers assume a 4xA100 (80GB) Dedicated pool with our recommended batching (dynamic batching with 20ms collection window) and prefix KV caching enabled for repeated contexts. The redwood-7b-quant numbers assume the same host count but smaller memory footprint per replica (so more replicas per machine in a Dedicated config). I can share the cluster spec doc if useful.
- Quality regressions: we have a small set of regressions vs. 13b on abstractive summarization for int8 variants. Typical deltas on our internal evals are ~0.6-1.5 ROUGE-L points and a ~0.02 BERTScore drop depending on prompt formulation. We'll run the regression check against your 100 prompts and attach a short report (ROUGE/BERTScore summary) to the benchmark export.

I've uploaded a short run playbook (run_instructions.pdf) that walks through how we'll execute the smoke runs and what metrics we'll report (TPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, model confidence scores, example failure cases). Link: https://app.redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/ACME-2451 and HubSpot record: https://hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-2451.

Proposed schedule:
- Mon/Tue: Acme shares 100 anonymized prompts (you said Monday).
- Wed: Redwood runs smoke quality + latency evals and returns CSV + short report.
- Thu: 30-minute readout to review tradeoffs and next steps.

Marissa (cc'd) will coordinate the run internally — Marissa, can you confirm available slots Wednesday for the benchmark run and whether Dylan should be looped in for the Dedicated cluster allocation?

Thanks,
Alex
